en: The Sūtra on Correspondence Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmaprabha of the Western Jin Dynasty.
The Buddha was staying in the kingdom of Śrāvastī and invited the bhikṣus; the bhikṣus arrived immediately. The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
The bhikṣu replied:
“Indeed, I have heard it from the Buddha.
The Buddha then spoke:
“Those who have not heard associate with those who have not heard; they resemble one another, gather together, correspond with one another, and find mutual approval.
Those who have heard much associate with those who have heard much; they resemble one another, gather together, correspond with one another, and find mutual approval.”
Those who are lustful associate with those who are lustful; they resemble one another, gather together, correspond with one another, and find mutual approval.
Those who are not lustful associate with those who are not lustful; they resemble one another, gather together, correspond with one another, and find mutual approval.
Those who harbor ill will associate with those who harbor ill will; they are of similar kind, they gather together, they correspond with one another, and they find mutual approval.
Those who do not harbor ill will associate with those who do not harbor ill will; they are of similar kind, they gather together, they correspond with one another, and they find mutual approval.
The foolish associate with the foolish; they are of similar kind, they gather together, they correspond with one another, and they find mutual approval.
The wise associate with the wise; they are of similar kind, they gather together, they correspond with one another, and they find mutual approval.
Those who practice generosity associate with those who practice generosity; they resemble one another, gather together, correspond with one another, and find mutual approval.
Those who are stingy and greedy associate with those who are stingy and greedy; they resemble one another, gather together, correspond with one another, and find mutual approval.
Those with few desires associate with those who have few desires; they are of similar kind, they gather together, they correspond with one another, and they find mutual approval.
Those with many desires associate with those who have many desires; they are of similar kind, they gather together, they correspond with one another, and they find mutual approval.

Those who do not observe the precepts associate with those who do not observe the precepts; they are of similar kind, they gather together, they correspond with one another, and they find mutual approval.
Those who observe the precepts associate with those who observe the precepts; they are of similar kind, they gather together, they correspond with one another, and they find mutual approval.
Those who are stingy associate with those who are stingy; they are of similar kind, they gather together, they correspond with one another, and they find mutual approval.
Those who are generous associate with those who are generous; they are of similar kind, they gather together, they correspond with one another, and they find mutual approval.
Those who are discontented associate with those who are discontented; they are of similar kind, they gather together, they correspond with one another, and they find mutual approval.
Those who are content associate with those who are content; they are of similar kind, they gather together, they correspond with one another, and they find mutual approval.

Those who do not maintain self-restraint associate with those who do not maintain self-restraint; they are of similar kind, they gather together, they respond to one another, and they find mutual approval.
Those who maintain self-restraint associate with those who maintain self-restraint; they are of similar kind, they gather together, they respond to one another, and they find mutual approval.
The Buddha said: "Monks!
A person of wisdom should thus discern these causal conditions: that which is to be practiced, they practice; that which is not to be practiced, they do not practice."
Thus spoke the Buddha.
The bhikṣus received and practiced it with focused attention.
This is the Sūtra on the Concordant and the Agreeable, as spoken by the Buddha.
